source.title: Towards Universality: Studying Mechanistic Similarity Across Language Model Architectures
source.authors: Junxuan Wang; Xu-Yang Ge; Wentao Shu; Qiong Tang; Yunhua Zhou; Zheng-Fu He; Xi-Peng Qiu

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAE feature matching to language models with different architectures and reports cross-architecture results relevant to SAE-recoverable features and their stability.
record.gate_note: The SAE matching and seed-variant results bear on V4 and V5. Neuron-baseline similarity and the induction-circuit path-patching results do not measure the versions' named claims, so they are not rows. The paper also discusses superposition as an assumption but does not test its geometry, sparsity transition, capacity account, or feature dimensionality.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on Pythia-160M, Mamba-130M and RWKV-169M and reports how reproducible SAE features are across SAE seeds, model seeds and architectures. This bears on V5's claim that dictionary features are stable, canonical units. It uses SAE recoverability (V4) as a premise and gives no quantitative test of it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude most SAE features are similar across Transformer and Mamba, and say the RWKV results confirm this. They find MPPC depends on feature complexity and identify an analogous induction circuit with an Off-by-One motif in Mamba. They caution that SAEs yield only a subset of true features and may capture combinations of features.
record.recipe_differences: This study compares SAE-derived features in trained language models using activation correlations; it does not use the toy-network superposition setup or measure its geometric predictions.
record.method_sensitivity: MPPC varies with comparison direction and feature complexity; the reverse Mamba-to-Pythia result is higher than the forward result, and simpler features tend to have higher MPPC.

fits_no_version.finding: The neuron baseline gives a mean MPPC of 0.30 across architectures, against 0.74 for SAE features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron-basis representations do not transfer across architectures, while SAE features do.

fits_no_version.finding: Matched SAE features sit at proportional depth across architectures (Pythia layer l maps to Mamba layer about 2l).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature hierarchy by depth is shared across architectures.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (listed in supplied metadata); the paper text says 'Preprint. Under Review.'
record.problems: Only a small set of architectures is evaluated. MPPC is a best-match correlation, not a demonstration that matched features are complete or canonical. The authors explicitly note that SAEs may miss rare features or represent combinations of true features. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the MPPC results.
record.rows_left_out: Neuron-baseline correlations and induction-circuit path-patching results are omitted because they do not measure V4 or V5 as defined. Other figure distributions and individual feature examples are not separately cataloged.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry, or sparsity transition.
No test of capacity competition or of dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.

Assumes SAEs recover sparse interpretable features. There is no quantitative test of recoverability or of features spreading across neurons. The neuron-vs-SAE contrast concerns cross-architecture matching, not superposition.
Completeness is not measured; the authors only state that SAEs yield a subset of features. SAE hyperparameters other than the seed were not varied.

missing.what: Features with cross-architecture MPPC below 0.2 are rated non-monosemantic or uninterpretable, with a clear boundary near 0.2.
Layer-wise MPPC distributions shift lower in later Pythia layers.
RWKV MPPC-difference interval of -0.45 to 0.06 versus the model-seed skyline.

record.verdict_notes: V4 links were removed from all rows: cross-model correlation of SAE features does not measure whether sparse features exist or are recoverable, and the study assumes SAE validity. All MPPC means are given without uncertainty. Peer-review status is unclear: the text says 'Preprint. Under Review'.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test superposition geometry, overlap, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry in toy networks.
Does not test whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests SAE feature extraction and similarity in Pythia, Mamba, and RWKV; does not test whether individual features are spread across many neurons.
Compares SAE feature similarity across SAE seeds and models, but does not establish that SAE features are complete or canonical units.
Does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Pythia-160M
rows.operation_detail: Measured maximum pairwise Pearson correlation (MPPC) between SAE features in Pythia and Mamba, forward direction.
rows.note: The paper reports that more than 30% of Pythia features have a matched Mamba feature with MPPC greater than 0.95.
rows.check: Bears on V5 (cross-model canonicality of SAE features), not V4: MPPC does not measure whether sparse features exist or are recoverable. A mean of 0.74 is clearly below perfect matching, so the state is partial, not observed.

source_check.correct: Mean cross-architecture SAE MPPC is 0.74; the reported neuron baseline is 0.30. Model-seed and SAE-seed skylines are 0.76 and 0.81.
source_check.problem: The baseline field omits the explicitly reported neuron baseline.

rows.subject: Pythia-160M
rows.operation_detail: Measured MPPC between Mamba and Pythia SAE features in the reverse direction.
rows.note: The appendix text states that reverse results outperform forward results, attributing this mainly to Mamba having more lower-level, simpler features.
rows.check: Same as r1. The subject is really the Mamba-130M SAE features matched to Pythia. A mean of 0.78 is below full matching. Drop V4.

source_check.correct: Subject: Mamba-130M SAE features; counterpart: Pythia-160M; direction: Mamba to Pythia; mean MPPC: 0.78.
source_check.problem: The source subject and counterpart are swapped for this reverse-direction measurement.

rows.subject: Pythia-160M
rows.operation_detail: Measured MPPC between features from two Pythia models trained with different random seeds.
rows.note: The paper uses this as a model-seed skyline.
rows.check: Model-seed skyline. A mean of 0.76 means SAE features are only partly reproduced across Pythia seeds. The reverse direction gives 0.75 (Fig 9b), which is not recorded.

rows.subject: Pythia-160M
rows.operation_detail: Measured MPPC between features from two SAEs trained on the same Pythia model.
rows.note: The paper describes this as the higher skyline, isolating differences from SAE training.
rows.check: The SAE-seed comparison is the direct stability test. A mean of 0.81 shows substantial but incomplete stability, not full canonicality. Only the seed was varied, although Sec 4.3.2 lists other hyperparameters.

rows.subject: Pythia-160M
rows.operation_detail: Compared cross-architecture MPPC with the Pythia model-seed MPPC for each Pythia feature.
rows.value: 90% of Pythia features fall in the interval -0.22 to 0.14; more than 60% have near-zero MPPC difference
rows.note: The authors interpret near-zero differences as features consistently present after the architecture changes.
rows.check: More than 60% of features have a near-zero difference from the model-seed skyline, but the baseline itself is only 0.76. Drop V4.

rows.subject: Pythia-160M
rows.operation_detail: Measured MPPC between Pythia SAE features and RWKV SAE features.
rows.note: The authors say the Mamba/Pythia conclusions are nearly applicable to RWKV/Pythia, while reporting lower numerical similarity than for Mamba.
rows.check: The RWKV mean of 0.65 is lower than for Mamba. The difference interval is -0.45 to 0.06 (Fig 11b), which is not recorded. Drop V4.

rows.subject: Pythia-160M
rows.operation_detail: Related automatically assigned feature-complexity scores to MPPC for model-seed and cross-architecture comparisons.
rows.measure: Association between feature complexity and MPPC
rows.value: The simpler a Pythia feature is, the more likely it is to match with a high Pearson correlation; the trend is weaker for the SAE-seed comparison.
rows.note: The authors report that feature complexity affects MPPC, complicating a direct interpretation of correlation as semantic similarity.
rows.check: Matching is high for simple token-level features and lower for complex ones, so stability depends on feature type. No numeric effect size is given, and the complexity scores were judged by GPT-4o.

relationships.condition: SAE seed variants on the same Pythia-160M model
relationships.reason: Mean MPPC between SAE seeds is 0.81, well short of identical features, so stability is incomplete (r4).
relationships.display_finding: Mean MPPC between SAE seeds was 0.81, well short of identical features.

relationships.reason: Mean MPPC is 0.76 for the model seed, 0.74/0.78 for Mamba and 0.65 for RWKV, so the same features are only partly recovered across models (r1, r2, r3, r5, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Mean MPPC was 0.76 against the Pythia seed variant, 0.74 and 0.78 for Mamba, and 0.65 for RWKV.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Across model seeds and architectures (Pythia vs Pythia seed, Mamba, RWKV)
source_check.reason: r1–r3 and r6 report incomplete activation correspondence: 0.74/0.78 for Pythia–Mamba, 0.76 across Pythia model seeds, and 0.65 for Pythia–RWKV. r5 shows architecture changes add relatively little discrepancy for many features.

relationships.reason: Simple features match with MPPC near 1; more than 30% of Pythia features have a Mamba match above 0.95 (r1, r7).
relationships.display_finding: These features matched with MPPC near 1, and more than 30% of Pythia features had a Mamba match above 0.95.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: Sections 5.1–5.2 and r7 associate simple token features with near-unit MPPC. r1 reports that more than 30% of all Pythia features have Mamba matches above 0.95; that percentage is not specifically a simple-feature subgroup rate.

relationships.reason: Complex features fall mostly in the 0.3–0.8 MPPC range, and MPPC shifts lower in later layers (Fig 8), so canonicality depends on feature type (r7).
relationships.display_finding: Complex features fell mostly in the 0.3–0.8 MPPC range, and matches weakened in later layers.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: r7 and Section 5.1 associate complex features with MPPC mostly between 0.3 and 0.8; Appendix B reports lower MPPC in later layers. This qualifies activation-pattern correspondence, while lower correlation can coexist with agreement in semantic theme.

relation.reason: Its SAE-seed comparison directly measures feature reproducibility; the architecture and model-seed comparisons provide additional evidence about feature correspondence relevant to V5.

tranche.reason: The study extends SAE feature comparisons to different language-model architectures and includes direct comparisons across SAE seeds and model seeds.

source_check.notes: MPPC measures activation correspondence, not completeness, unique dictionary recovery, causal identity, or direct transfer; the authors explicitly caution that SAEs may miss true features or combine them. Figure 9b additionally reports reverse Pythia model-seed MPPC of 0.75.
